q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a glass tumbler?
title: Glass tumbler carbon footprint per piece
short: Most of a tumbler's footprint comes from melting glass: divide the furnace fuel and plant electricity by good pieces packed, then add batch materials and packing. Count CO2 released by soda ash and limestone in the batch separately from fuel.
audience: Glassware makers and hotel and retail buyers

ul: Furnace fuel, often natural gas or furnace oil.
Pressing or blowing machines and fire polishing.
Sand, soda ash, limestone and cullet.

p: Report per piece with its weight. A heavier tumbler takes more glass and more melting energy.

example.title: Worked example: glass tumbler unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 378,500 / 1,500,000 = 0.252 kg CO2 per piece
Add batch process CO2 and packing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
